To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HIV-derived lentiviral gene transfer vectors that display on their surface a T cell-acting polypeptide derived of a T-cell-activating antibody can transduce human primary resting T cells with high efficiency.
lentiviral vectors display a T cell activating polypeptide that increases gene transfer into human peripheral blood lymphocytes by up to 48% without addition of PML activation stimuli.
surface-engineered HIV-1-derived vectors display a single chain antibody that activates the target cells, and that these vectors significantly increase gene delivery in primary lymphocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel lentiviral gene transfer systems for human gene therapy applications.
the development and characterization of lentiviral vectors with enhanced transduction efficiency of nondividing primary cells.
the development of novel gene transfer methods for the treatment of genetic and immunological diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the surface display of OKT3-derived single-chain antibody on HIV-1-derived vector particles significantly increases gene transfer into primary human lymphocytes, and that this approach can be used to activate target cells during lentivirus-mediated gene transfer.
surface-engineered HIV-1-based lentiviral vectors are a valuable tool for the transduction of resting lymphocytes.
the use of lentiviral vectors displaying the T cell-activat- ing single-chain antibody OKT3 is an efficient and safe method for gene transfer into primary lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OKT3-displayed vectors can transduce primary lymphocytes in vitro, and that this may be of potential therapeutic benefit.
we developed a novel strategy to improve transduction of resting T cells by surface display of T cell activation molecules on the viral surface, which could be applied for gene transfer applications.
the OKT3-displayed HIV-1 vectors efficiently transduced primary lymphocytes without addition of PRL activation stimuli during infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the surface display of a T-cell-activating single chain antibody (scAb) on lentiviral vectors allows efficient gene delivery into resting human peripheral blood lymphocytes in the absence of exogenous cell-activating stimuli.
the surface-engineered lentivirus vectors significantly improved transduction of primary human lymphocytes by activating target cells.
surface-engineered retroviral and lentiviral vectors can be used to improve gene transfer into primary lymphocytes.
